info.name: TW Retail pricing API
info.description:
Procurement price for a used two-wheeler (app/ FastAPI service, model **Pure MAXFIT + Optuna settings**, exported 2026-11-02).

**Start**
1. Import this collection and `TW_Retail_Pricing_API.postman_environment.json`; pick the environment *TW Retail pricing API - local*.
2. In the environment, put the password in **Current value** of `password` (Current values are not shared or exported).
3. Start the server (`python -m uvicorn app.main:app --port 8000`, or `docker compose up`) and send any request. The collection logs in by itself (collection pre-request script) and keeps the token for its lifetime.

**Order** (as the web form): Mfg years → Makes → Models → Variants → Cities → Predict price. Copy the chosen values into the collection variables below; the defaults are a working example (Royal Enfield Classic 350, Standard, 2020, Pune).

| Variable | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `baseUrl` | `http://127.0.0.1:8000` | server address |
| `username` | `admin` | login user |
| `password` | `` | set it in the environment's Current value |
| `token` | `` | set by the login (automatic) |
| `tokenExpiresAt` | `` | set by the login (automatic) |
| `mfg_year` | `2020` | from Mfg years |
| `make` | `Royal Enfield` | from Makes |
| `model_key` | `royalenfield|classic 350` | from Models (not the name) |
| `variant_id` | `BW-V136` | from Variants |
| `city` | `Pune` | from Cities |

Errors: `401` = no / expired token or wrong login; `422` = bad input, the reason is in `detail`.
Run the whole collection (Runner) to test a server: every request has tests, the error cases expect their error codes.
Built by `scripts/build_postman_collection.py`; example responses are real responses of the app.

exec: // Logs in when there is no token or it has expired; the token goes into the collection variable 'token'.

console.warn('Set the password variable (environment, Current value) to log in automatically.');

request.description: No login needed. Shows the served model and the ± band.

OAuth2 password form: username + password → JWT (HS256), valid 8 hours by default (TWR_TOKEN_MINUTES). The test script stores the token in the collection variable `token`; every other request sends it as `Authorization: Bearer {{token}}`.

Not needed by hand: the collection logs in by itself when the token is missing or expired.
The user the token belongs to.
Mfg years the form offers, newest first. Tick `model_key` / `variant_id` to limit it to a model or variant.
The years in which this variant was on sale (1 year before launch to 1 year after discontinuation).

request.description:
Price for a used bike, as of today.

| Field | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `make` | yes | from Makes |
| `model_key` | yes | from Models; must belong to `make` |
| `variant_id` | no | from Variants; null = not known → the model's cheapest variant for that year (as in training) |
| `mfg_year` | yes | up to the quote year; within the variant's catalogue years |
| `owner_count` | no (1) | 1-4; 4 = 4 or more |
| `odometer_km` | yes | 0 - 2,000,000 |
| `city` | yes | from Cities |
| `quote_date` | no (today) | YYYY-MM-DD |

Returns `predicted_price` (rounded to ₹100), `price_band_5k` (± ₹5,000), `model_range` (90%) and `model_ranges` (80 / 90 / 95%), `training_reference` (median price of similar training bikes), the 24 `features` used, and `warnings`.
